The two variables are strongly correlated (r = 0.88), so a causal link clearly exists and D is out. I didn't run a direction test on the data. I picked the direction on physical grounds. Sea-level pressure reflects the mass of the air column above the surface. By the hydrostatic relationship, more mass raises the geopotential height of upper-level pressure surfaces. That makes B more likely than A, and C is unlikely because the physical relationship runs mainly one way.

ANSWER: B
